content: Dr. Jill Stein, a physician and activist affiliated with the Green-Rainbow Party, resides in Lexington, Massachusetts. She is a member of the boards of Greater Boston Physicians for Social Responsibility and Mass Voters for Fair Elections. Additionally, she has been actively involved with the Massachusetts Coalition for Healthy Communities. In 2002, Dr. Stein ran as the Green-Rainbow Party candidate for Governor of Massachusetts. She received 5% of the total vote in that election. Following her gubernatorial campaign, Dr. Stein ran for a seat in the Massachusetts House of Representatives in 2004, representing the Ninth Middlesex District. She was endorsed by State Representative Jay R. Kaufman. Despite her efforts, she garnered 9% of the vote, trailing behind the Democratic incumbent Thomas M., who secured 6% more of the vote than her. In March 2005, Dr. Stein was elected to a Town Meeting seat in Precinct 2, located in North Waltham, Middlesex County, during the local elections. She received 6% of the total vote in this election. On March 4, 2006, Dr. Stein was nominated by the Green-Rainbow Party as their candidate for Secretary of the Commonwealth during the party's statewide nominating convention. She was the sole challenger to the three-term Democratic incumbent, Bill Galvin. The general election took place on November 7, 2006. Dr. Stein performed strongly in this head-to-head contest, receiving 353,551 votes, which accounted for 18% of the total vote. This result marked the best performance by a Green Party candidate running for Secretary of State in any state to date.
